notes.title: Ryder Is Live in Steam Next Fest – With a Special Demo Update!
notes.content:
Hello, friends!

We’re excited to share that Ryder is officially live in Steam Next Fest, and we’ve released a special demo update just for the event!

For this week only, you can:
🔹 Solve a brand new puzzle
🔹 Meet a brand new creature
🔹 Discover limited-time variants of existing creatures—hidden throughout the world

If you’ve played the demo before, now’s the perfect time to revisit it. And if you’re new to Ryder, welcome! This is a non-violent, creature-collecting puzzle adventure where every puzzle solved brings a new creature back into the world—and slowly restores life to the land.

Later this week, we’ll also be announcing Ryder’s release date, so stay tuned for that reveal!

Until then, we’d love to hear what you think of the update—and if you manage to find any of the special variants, feel free to post them and tag us. We may even highlight a few in a future post on our social channels!

Thanks so much for the support, and happy exploring!
—Arlin & Elle

notes.title: The Ryder Demo Just Got an Update!
notes.content:
Thanks so much to everyone who played the first version of the Ryder demo and sent us your thoughts—it’s been amazing to hear from you!

We’ve just pushed an update that focuses on streamlining the experience and adding more of what makes Ryder fun. Here’s what’s new:

Puzzle flow is faster and smoother—less backtracking, quicker start, more polished creature selection process

 Creatures are faster and more responsive
 You can now try out actual creature abilities in the demo! You'll get to try the wind burst and wind jump mechanics
 Improved framerate, bug fixes, and better UI behavior
 The creatures have eyes now. 👀
 If you haven’t tried the demo yet, now’s a great time! You’ll explore a peaceful autumnal forest, solve 7 puzzles (4 new from previous version), and meet 5 playable creatures (3 new from previous version).


Additionally, here is Elle, the Creative Director, explaining Ryder in detail:
Everything You Need to Know About Ryder

Don’t forget to Wishlist and Follow us to stay in the loop!

Important Note: Unfortunately at this time the Ryder Demo will not be playable on Steam Deck. We are working to resolve the issue and we hope to support it soon! f you run into any other issues, please let us know via this Google Form. And come chat with us in the Discord—we’d love to hear what you think!

Thanks again for supporting our little game.

— Arlin and Elle
Yellow Tree Games

notes.title: Drakes, Dragons, and Pumpkins Oh My
notes.content:
Happy February! 

We’re continuing to develop Ryder and are thrilled to introduce you to three dragon-like creatures you’ll meet—and play as!—on your journey.

The Drumpkin

As its name suggests, this adorable, pumpkin-shaped dragon feels right at home in Goldenwood’s autumnal landscapes. With its Wind Jump ability, the Drumpkin can help you reach higher locations in puzzles—a handy companion for exploring!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45278192/f5eb8405605cd19fb33f5bd455c0e252056854b3.png

The Snapdragon

Among the tall grasses of Emerald Valley, you might catch glimpses of bright pink wings decorated with flowers. The Snapdragon loves flowers so much, it grew its own! Beyond its charm, its Teleportation Flowers ability will be key to solving puzzles in creative ways.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45278192/50050b206e3a680fb0e5f8f84f9c1623b227deec.png

The Driftdrake

Gliding through the snowy forests of the Silver Pines, the Driftdrake is a frosty blue dragon with a snowflake-tipped tail. But its chill isn’t just for looks—its Freeze ability allows you to hold objects in place for puzzle-solving..

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45278192/85abf940ebdb5eaa71bddc212d78157914b04d0d.png
 
In case you missed it… the Ryder demo is live!
- Explore a stunning autumnal forest
- Solve 7 unique puzzles
- Discover 25 creature variants

🎥 Check out our new gameplay trailer! 👇

Wishlist & follow Ryder on Steam to stay updated on our progress!

Thank you so much for playing our demo! 
Arlin and Elle

notes.title: Meet the husband and wife duo behind Ryder
notes.content:
Hello everyone! We’re Arlin and Elle at Yellow Tree Games. We're a husband-and-wife team united by our shared love for art, programming, and video games. Through this passion, we created Ryder, a creature-collecting puzzle adventure with a world brimming with unique, fantastical creatures.

Crafting a Vision for Ryder
The idea for Ryder began with a simple goal: a low-poly creature-collecting game that felt as distinct as it was immersive. Elle’s love for drawing animals and our mutual appreciation for classic creature-collecting games steered us in this direction from the start. Our goal was to create a nostalgic visual experience with a high level of detail, striking a balance between retro charm and modern design. We chose a low-poly art style rendered through Unreal Engine’s Lumen system, achieving both technical and artistic goals. Being a small team, we needed designs that were detailed enough to feel unique yet manageable enough to develop within a realistic timeframe. By focusing on each creature’s essentials, we can build a diverse and vibrant world without overstretching.

Shaping Ryder’s Core Gameplay
At the heart of Ryder are two core principles: each creature should add something new and distinct to gameplay, and collecting creatures should involve not just collecting, but understanding their utility. We experimented with different gameplay loops—survival, mini-games, racing, resource gathering, and even creature farming—before realizing that creature-driven puzzles best reflected our vision. Puzzles became the perfect way to spotlight each creature’s unique traits and give players meaningful interactions.
We also made a deliberate design choice to allow players to become the creatures themselves rather than just ride or mount them. This unique perspective lets players experience the world through each creature's eyes, with puzzles tailored to the physicality and abilities of every creature. This decision added depth to gameplay, letting players explore the world from different perspectives and engage with puzzles in a way that feels natural and satisfying.


Building a Creature-Rich Puzzle World
In Ryder, “distinct addition” means each creature offers unique trade-offs that shape the puzzle experience. For example, two creatures might share the same ability, but one might be as large as an elephant while the other is a small mouse. The elephant-sized creature can trigger weight-sensitive mechanisms, while the mouse can fit into narrow spaces. Ryder’s puzzles often require balancing these abilities, such as using a heavier creature to open a path and then switching to a smaller one to progress through tighter areas.
While puzzles are central to Ryder, we wanted the game to feel like an open, exploratory world rather than a series of back-to-back challenges. Players are encouraged to venture off the main path, uncover new creatures, and experience the freedom of roaming in the woods with their favorites. Our bestiary system allows hardcore collectors to hunt down every puzzle and creature, while casual players can advance through organic exploration at their own pace.


The Road to Release
We’re thrilled to be working toward a 2025 release, with plans to include over 60 creatures and more than 100 puzzles. Designing puzzles that work seamlessly with each creature’s traits has been a fun challenge, and we can’t wait to share more details on how these mechanics will unfold.
Thank you for following our journey with Ryder! We’ll dive deeper into the puzzle mechanics and other aspects of the game in upcoming dev logs. In the meantime, you can follow us on our social channels for sneak peeks and updates as we bring Ryder to life.
